output.brief:
COO — the failures come from Pellacott's 2026 valves, not from the new installers or firmware 4.2.

Matched by unit serial, Pellacott 2026 valves fail at about 41 per 1,000 whichever installer and firmware are involved; Durrant-Hale valves in the same groups sit at 5–7. Brenmoor's helium retest found 11% of never-installed Pellacott 2026 valves leaking at the seat, versus 1% for 2025 and 0% for Durrant-Hale. Pellacott's score rose because its certificates became complete and all-pass, but the independent visit found its leak rig out of service since 9 January, no other test equipment, and certificates repeating the same four value sequences. The tests those certificates describe almost certainly did not happen. I'm about 90% sure.

Unresolved: seal change versus Line 3 move as the cause, and whether other suppliers' records are unreliable.

Do now: keep the six lots held; don't release on fresh paperwork. Quarantine 2026-built Pellacott stock, suspend dock-to-stock, and release only valves passing Brenmoor's helium test; ask Durrant-Hale about extra supply. Drop the installer plan and chargebacks. Then run a seal-versus-line trial, spot-check other suppliers' rig logs, and tie scores to logs.
